title: Rational purity scalar squares at the two exchange endpoints
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a_0\geq1$, and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^{a_0}}$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure. Let $X,X',Y,Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $u:X'\to X$, $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $v:Y'\to Y$ form a Cartesian square $f\circ u=v\circ f'$ [def-pc-base-change], where $f$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ and $v$ is arbitrary. Use $\mathcal C_R(W)=D^b_c(W,R)$, for $R=E,L$, in the raw rationalization convention [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], derived pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and exact scalar extension $T_W=T_{L/E,W}$ with its specified pullback comparisons $p_{h,M}:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}Lh_E^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_L^*T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}M$ from [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Put $D_W^R(M)=M(d)[2d]$ and $H_{h,R}=D_{\mathrm{source}(h)}^RLh_R^*$ for $h=f,f'$. Let $q_{W,M}:T_WD_W^EM\xrightarrow{\sim}D_W^LT_WM$ be the canonical tensor, twist and shift comparison, and put
$$a_{h,M}=D_{\mathrm{source}(h)}^L(p_{h,M})\circ q_{\mathrm{source}(h),Lh_E^*M}.$$

All four schemes are Noetherian, finite-dimensional, with $\ell$ invertible; $f'$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$, also for empty $X'$. Every object of $\mathcal C_E(W)$ has a representative in the derived-complete integral category $D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$ with a single Tor interval for its finite reductions, and $Lv_E^*K$ is represented by the integral pullback of such a representative for $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$.

Use $G_{h,R}=Rh_R^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $\gamma_{h,R}:H_{h,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,R}$ be the rationalization of the simultaneous integral family in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], with the rational purity convention [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Let $b_{h,M}:T G_{h,E}M\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,L}TM$ be the rationalization of that family's counit-normalized comparison (the transpose of scalar extension of the exceptional counit via inverse compact-support scalar comparison). Then $a_h$ above is precisely the rationalized comparison $a$ of that family, and for every rational object $M$ on the target of $h$ one has
$$b_{h,M}\circ T(\gamma_{h,E,M})=\gamma_{h,L,TM}\circ a_{h,M}.\tag{P}$$
This equation and naturality hold for all localized morphisms, with the localized unit, successive-extension and shift equations of that integral family.

For $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$ put
$$s_{R,K}=Lu_R^*(\gamma_{f,R,K}^{-1}),\qquad t^{\gamma}_{R,K}=\gamma_{f',R,Lv_R^*K},$$
$$r_{A,K}=Lu_L^*(a_{f,K})\circ p_{u,H_{f,E}K},\qquad r_{B,K}=H_{f',L}(p_{v,K})\circ a_{f',Lv_E^*K},$$
$$\beta_{A,K}=Lu_L^*(b_{f,K})\circ p_{u,G_{f,E}K},\qquad \beta_{B,K}=G_{f',L}(p_{v,K})\circ b_{f',Lv_E^*K}.$$
Here $s_L$ and $t^\gamma_L$ in the following equations are evaluated at $T_YK$. The two endpoint squares are
$$r_{A,K}\circ T_{X'}(s_{E,K})=s_{L,T_YK}\circ\beta_{A,K},\tag{A}$$
$$\beta_{B,K}\circ T_{X'}(t^\gamma_{E,K})=t^\gamma_{L,T_YK}\circ r_{B,K}.\tag{B}$$
They are equalities of natural transformations in $K$. For an identity coefficient extension all endpoint comparison maps $r_A,r_B,\beta_A,\beta_B$ are identities under the canonical identifications. For nested finite fields $E\subset F\subset L$ each of these four comparison families $w$ satisfies the tower equation
$$w_{L/E,K}\circ\alpha^{\mathrm{in}}_K=\alpha^{\mathrm{out}}_K\circ w_{L/F,T_{F/E}K}\circ T_{L/F}(w_{F/E,K}),$$
where $\alpha^{\mathrm{in}},\alpha^{\mathrm{out}}$ are the source and target tensor associators, carried through the displayed pullback or exceptional functors. Equations (P), (A), (B) respect these identifications and the canonical shift comparisons $w_{K[1]}=w_K[1]$; no extra identification of the exceptional comparison is allowed.

proof.text: Apply rational_lattice_adic_base to each vertex, and the first clause of rational_lattice_adic_domain to the actual integral object retained by every raw rational object. Its localization is literally that rational object. For v use constructibleIntegralPullback on that same representative, apply the first domain clause to its constructibility proof, and use the object equation of rationalDerivedPullback_existsUnique. No change of lattices or smoothness hypothesis on v is used.
Use MorphismProperty.of_isPullback with the given square for smooth relative dimension d, separatedness, local finite type and quasi-compactness. These properties include the empty-source cases.

For each supplied integral family, unpack rationalScalarComparisonIdentification and put its shift, normalized localization, scalar, purity, counit-mate, unit and tower data into LocalizedFamily. Every field is the corresponding supplied conclusion; the maps are not replaced.

Apply twistedPullbackCoefficientCoherence to the commuting square with the just-proved base conditions. Keep only the unit, tower and shift laws of the actual pullback scalar comparisons p_u and p_v. Remove the identity equality transports in its unit and associator formulas by proof irrelevance. These are precisely the specified scalar units, associators and shifts in the endpoint statement.

For a composite F followed by U, its pasted comparison has component p_U(FK) followed by U(a_F(K)); this follows by evaluating the five stated associators and whiskerings. Invert the purity square by canceling the image of gamma.hom. Naturality of p_u at gamma.inv, followed by the inverse purity square under pullback, gives squareA. For squareB apply the forward purity square at Lv*(K), followed by naturality of the final gamma at p_v. Extensionality promotes these component equations to equalities of natural transformations.

Prove the generic pasting unit law by mapping the first factor unit equation through U and then applying the second. For the tower law, substitute the U tower equation and then map the F tower equation through the last U; naturality of the middle U comparison at the first F comparison interchanges the middle factors. Functoriality identifies the resulting word with the two pasted comparisons. Apply this to both alternatives of both endpoints. Shift compatibility follows from the Mathlib instances for composition, associators and whiskering, using the recorded factor shift structures. The inverse-gamma shift follows from compatibility of inverse isomorphisms; whiskering gives shiftS and shiftT.
